9.1: To you who do not cavil I shall declare this most profound secret of knowledge and realisation, knowing which you will be freed.
9.2: This is the king of sciences and the king of secrets — supreme purifier, directly realisable, easy to practise, imperishable.
9.3: Those without faith in this teaching do not attain Me and return to the round of death.
9.4: All this world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest form; all beings dwell in Me, but I do not dwell in them.
9.5: And yet beings do not dwell in Me — behold My divine mystery: My Self sustains beings without dwelling in them.
9.6: As the mighty wind moves everywhere yet rests in space, so all beings rest in Me.
9.7: At the end of a cycle all beings return to My nature; at the beginning I send them forth again.
9.8: Controlling My own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude, helpless under the sway of nature.
9.9: These actions do not bind Me, seated as one indifferent, unattached to them.
9.10: Under My oversight, nature produces the moving and unmoving; for this reason the world revolves.
9.11: Fools disregard Me clothed in human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of beings.
9.12: Of vain hopes, vain actions and vain knowledge, they are possessed of a deluded, demonic nature.
9.13: But the great souls, taking refuge in the divine nature, worship Me single-mindedly, knowing Me as the imperishable source.
9.14: Always glorifying Me, striving with firm resolve, bowing down with devotion, they worship Me ever steadfast.
9.15: Others worship by the sacrifice of knowledge, as one, as manifold, as facing everywhere in My universal form.
9.16: I am the ritual, the sacrifice, the offering, the herb, the mantra, the butter, the fire, and the act of offering.
9.17: I am the father, mother, sustainer and grandsire of this world, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the three Vedas.
9.18: I am the goal, supporter, lord, witness, abode, refuge, friend, origin, dissolution, foundation, treasure-house and imperishable seed.
9.19: I give heat, hold back and send forth rain; I am immortality and death, being and non-being.
9.20: Knowers of the Vedas who drink the soma and seek heaven attain the world of the gods and enjoy divine pleasures.
9.21: Having enjoyed that vast heaven, their merit exhausted, they enter the mortal world again — desire-driven, they come and go.
9.22: But to those who worship Me alone with undivided thought, ever steadfast, I secure what they lack and preserve what they have.
9.23: Even devotees of other gods who worship with faith worship Me alone, though not in the proper way.
9.24: I am the enjoyer and Lord of all sacrifices; those who do not know Me in truth fall back.
9.25: Worshippers of gods go to the gods, of ancestors to ancestors, of spirits to spirits — My worshippers come to Me.
9.26: The famous verse of simplicity: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water — offered with devotion, I accept from the pure-hearted.
9.27: Whatever you do, eat, offer, give or practise as austerity — do it as an offering to Me.
9.28: So you will be freed from the bonds of action and its good and evil fruits, and liberated, come to Me.
9.29: I am the same in all beings; none is hateful or dear to Me — but those who worship Me with devotion are in Me, and I in them.
9.30: Even the worst evildoer, if he worships Me with undivided devotion, is to be regarded as righteous, for he has rightly resolved.
9.31: That devotee quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace — know that My devotee never perishes.
9.32: All who take refuge in Me, whatever their birth or station, attain the supreme goal.
9.33: How much more the holy and the devoted royal sages — having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship Me.
9.34: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow to Me; thus united, you will come to Me.
